name: Jonha Falls
description: Jonha Falls, also called Gautam Dhara, drops about 150 feet on the Radhu river near Jonha village, 40 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Purulia highway. A Buddha statue stands at the site, and the fall marks a fault line of the Ranchi plateau. Sita Falls is close by.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Purulia road; Jonha railway station on the Ranchi-Muri line is nearby.
practical_notes: Best visited between October and February. Steps lead down to the viewing area; carry water and watch your footing on wet rock.

name: Palamu Fort
description: Palamu Fort comprises an old and a new fort on the bank of the Auranga river inside Palamu Tiger Reserve, about 5 km from Betla National Park. The older fort was built by Chero ruler Pratap Rai (1628-1658) and the newer one by his successor Medini Rai (1658-1674). Their walls still carry marks of cannon fire, and the new fort's carved Nagpuri gate is notable.
how_to_reach: In Latehar district, about 5 km from Betla National Park; reached by road via Daltonganj or Latehar.
practical_notes: The fort lies inside a protected forest area; check current access permissions at Betla before setting out.

name: Baidyanath Dham
description: Baidyanath Dham in Deoghar is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva and a major pilgrimage centre, believed to mark where the heart of Sati fell. The ancient temple is also called Ravaneshwar Mahadev. During Shravan, large numbers of kanwariyas carry Ganges water here on foot.
how_to_reach: Deoghar is connected by rail and road; the temple is in the town centre, about 1.5 km from Naulakha Temple.
practical_notes: Expect heavy crowds in Shravan (July-August). Follow temple dress and queue rules; mobile phones and leather items are restricted inside.

name: Amadubi
description: Amadubi, a village in the Dhalbhumgarh area of East Singhbhum, is known for Paitkar painting, a traditional scroll art form. Artists paint narrative scrolls on paper and cloth using natural colours, and the village has become a rural tourism and craft stop promoted by the state tourism department.
how_to_reach: In East Singhbhum district, reached by road from Jamshedpur via Dhalbhumgarh.
practical_notes: Visit during daylight hours and ask before photographing artists at work; Paitkar scrolls can be bought directly from workshops.

name: Satsang Ashram
description: The Satsang Ashram in Deoghar was established by followers of Sri Anukul Chandra Thakur and is a spiritual centre that draws devotees from across the region. Visitors come for prayer, quiet reflection and the ashram's community life.
how_to_reach: In Deoghar town, a short drive from the railway station and Baidyanath Dham.
practical_notes: Dress modestly and keep noise low; check ashram timings for darshan and congregational prayers.

name: Netarhat Sunrise Point
description: Netarhat, about 156 km west of Ranchi in Latehar district, is a hill station known for its pine and sal forests, cool air and sweeping valley views. The sunrise point looks east over the Chhotanagpur plateau, and the town is also famous for its sunsets and Netarhat School.
how_to_reach: About 156 km from Ranchi by road via Kuru or Latehar; regular buses run to Netarhat.
practical_notes: Mornings are cold even in summer; carry a jacket. Reach the point before dawn for the best light.

name: Saranda Forest
description: Saranda, whose name means land of seven hundred hills, is one of Asia's largest sal forests, spread across roughly 900 sq km in West Singhbhum. It shelters elephants and rich sal, mahua and kusum vegetation, and is home to Ho communities. Chaibasa is the main gateway.
how_to_reach: About 122 km from Jamshedpur; the main entry is via Chaibasa, 60 km from Jamshedpur.
practical_notes: This is a sensitive forest and mining region; travel with local guidance, carry permits if required and avoid unmarked trails.

name: Dassam Falls
description: Dassam Falls, also called Dassam Ghagh, is formed by the Kanchi river falling about 144 feet near Taimara village, 45 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata road. The Kanchi is a tributary of the Subarnarekha, and the fall is surrounded by forested slopes.
how_to_reach: About 45 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Jamshedpur road, near Taimara.
practical_notes: Best from October to January. Swimming is unsafe; stay behind the barriers on the rocks.

name: Panchghagh Falls
description: Panchghagh Falls near Khunti takes its name from the five visible streams that make up the fall, also called Panch Dhara. It lies about 50 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Chaibasa road and 14 km from Khunti, and is a popular picnic spot.
how_to_reach: About 50 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Chaibasa road via the Simdega route, 14 km from Khunti.
practical_notes: The flow is strongest after the monsoon. Weekends and holidays are busy; carry your own food and water.

name: Lower Ghaghri Falls
description: Lower Ghaghri Falls lies 4-5 km below Upper Ghaghri and about 10-12 km from Netarhat bus stand, reached through dense forest. The stream drops about 32 feet, and the surrounding canopy is thick enough to filter the sun.
how_to_reach: About 10-12 km from Netarhat bus stand by road and a short walk.
practical_notes: The approach path can be slippery; go with a local guide and avoid the forest after dark.

name: Lodh Falls
description: Lodh Falls in Latehar district is claimed as Jharkhand's highest waterfall, where the Burha river drops about 468 feet between two hills. Remains of a colonial-era bungalow used by British officials still stand nearby. It is about 61 km from Netarhat.
how_to_reach: About 61 km from Netarhat and 14 km northwest of Orsapat via Mahuadar; road access is rough in places.
practical_notes: The last stretch is remote; arrange a vehicle and local guide in advance and carry food and water.

name: Mirchaiya Falls
description: Mirchaiya Falls lies about 3 km from Garu block in Latehar district, inside the Betla tiger landscape. It is formed by a tributary of the North Koel river, and a dark granite outcrop stands like a dome beside the fall. The fall is beside the Garu-Netarhat road.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from Garu; buses run between Daltonganj and Garu.
practical_notes: Considered one of the safer falls in the region, but the rocks are still slippery. Food and lodging are available in Garu.

name: Betla National Park
description: Betla National Park lies about 25 km off the Ranchi-Daltonganj road in Latehar district and forms part of the Palamu Tiger Reserve. Its forests shelter tiger, leopard, elephant and deer, and the park has a museum, forest rest houses and a tree house. Chero king Medini Rai's fort stands nearby.
how_to_reach: About 156 km from Ranchi to the turn-off, then 25 km to Betla; jeep safaris are arranged at the park.
practical_notes: Safari timings are fixed by the forest department; book ahead in peak season and carry binoculars.

name: Birsa Deer Park, Kalamati
description: Birsa Deer Park at Kalamati in Ranchi district is a small wildlife park and breeding centre for spotted deer and other local species. It offers a short nature outing close to the city.
how_to_reach: At Kalamati in Ranchi district, reached by road from the city.
practical_notes: Go early morning or late afternoon when animals are active; check local opening hours.
address: Birsa Deer Park, Kalamati, Ranchi, Jharkhand

name: Tenughat Dam
description: Tenughat Dam on the Damodar river near Petarwar in Bokaro district stands about 166 feet high and spreads over roughly 30 sq km. Its 29-km canal supplies water to the Bokaro steel plant, and boating is available on the reservoir.
how_to_reach: About 75 km from Bokaro on the Bokaro-Ramgarh road (NH 33); turn right at Petarwar.
practical_notes: The reservoir area is best visited in the cooler months; confirm boating availability locally.

name: Tilaiya Dam
description: Tilaiya Dam on the Barakar river in Koderma district was built under the Damodar Valley Corporation's programme. It lies about 22 km south of Koderma and 150 km from Ranchi, and its wooded shoreline is a quiet picnic and viewing spot.
how_to_reach: About 22 km south of Koderma; Koderma is the nearest railway station, about 19 km away.
practical_notes: Access to the dam area can be restricted; check with local authorities before travelling.

name: Khandoli
description: Khandoli, about 10 km from Giridih town, combines a small dam, hill, amusement park and water sports area within a compact radius. The lake attracts migratory birds from northern Asia, the Himalayan belt, Africa and Australia, and an adventure festival is held here in October.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Giridih town by road; autos and taxis are available.
practical_notes: Boating and adventure activities depend on the season; the lake is busiest during the October festival.

name: Kiriburu
description: Kiriburu in West Singhbhum district is a hill station and mining town set among green forests, known for its cool climate and views of the surrounding ranges. It is about 257 km from Ranchi and is often paired with Megahatuburu.
how_to_reach: About 257 km from Ranchi via Tatanagar; the nearest railway station is Barajamda, about 24 km away.
practical_notes: Much of the area is connected with iron-ore mining; check access to viewpoints with local hosts.

name: Burudih Lake
description: Burudih Lake in Ghatshila block of East Singhbhum is a small reservoir ringed by low hills and forest, popular for motor and paddle boating. The surrounding hills form part of an elephant corridor linking the Dalma range with Midnapore in West Bengal.
how_to_reach: Nearest railway station is Ghatshila, about 136 km from Ranchi; autos run from Ghatshila to the lake.
practical_notes: Boating is subject to water levels and weather. Combine with a Ghatshila day trip.

name: Vibhuti Bhushan House
description: The house of Bengali writer Vibhuti Bhushan Bandyopadhyay, author of Pather Panchali, stands at Ghatshila in East Singhbhum. The writer lived here, and the house preserves the memory of a literary figure whose novels were translated widely and adapted for cinema by Satyajit Ray.
how_to_reach: At Ghatshila, about 136 km from Ranchi; Ghatshila has a railway station on the Kharagpur-Tatanagar line.
practical_notes: The house is a heritage property; check opening hours locally and ask before entering private areas.
address: Vibhuti Bhushan House, East Singhbum, Jharkhand

name: Naulakha Temple
description: Naulakha Temple stands about 1.5 km from Baidyanath Dham in Deoghar. The grand Radha-Krishna temple was built by Rani Charushila of the Pathurighata royal family at a reported cost of nine lakh rupees, which gives the temple its name.
how_to_reach: In Deoghar town, about 1.5 km from Baidyanath Dham; reached by auto or on foot.
practical_notes: Combine with Baidyanath Dham and Nandan Pahar on the same day; expect crowds during festivals.

name: Nandan Pahar
description: Nandan Pahar is a low hill on the edge of Deoghar with a temple and a landscaped recreation area at its foot. It is a popular family stop and offers views over the town.
how_to_reach: On the Deoghar-Dumka side of town, a short drive from Baidyanath Dham.
practical_notes: Check local timings for the temple and any rides; mornings are quieter.

name: Basukinath Dham
description: Basukinath Dham, about 25 km from Dumka on the Dumka-Deoghar road, is an ancient Shiva temple linked to the churning of the ocean, when Vasuki was used as the rope. Pilgrims visiting Baidyanath Dham often complete their journey here.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Dumka on the Dumka-Deoghar road; buses and taxis ply the route.
practical_notes: The temple is busiest in Shravan; dress modestly and follow queue arrangements.

name: Parasnath Hill
description: Parasnath, at 4,480 feet the highest hill in Jharkhand, is the Jain pilgrimage site of Sammed Shikhar. Twenty of the twenty-four Tirthankaras are believed to have attained nirvana here, and their footprints are enshrined at the summit. It is about 35 km from Giridih.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Giridih; Parasnath railway station is 11 km east, and the climb from Madhuban takes several hours.
practical_notes: The ascent involves a long flight of steps and is closed to some visitors during certain Jain observances; check before climbing.

name: Sun Temple, Bundu
description: The Sun Temple near Bundu, about 35 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata road, is a marble temple built in the form of Surya's chariot with eighteen wheels and seven horses. It was built by the Sanskriti Vihar organisation, and a Tusu Mela is held here on 25 January.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata road near Bundu.
practical_notes: The temple is especially busy around Tusu Mela in January; check timings before visiting.

name: Maluti Temples
description: Maluti, a village on the Chila river near the West Bengal border about 55 km from Dumka, is known as the village of temples. It has 108 temples, many with ancient stone sculptures, built under the patronage of the Mall kings of Bishnupur. The Archaeological Survey has surveyed the village for conservation.
how_to_reach: About 55 km from Dumka; the nearest railway station is Rampurhat in West Bengal.
practical_notes: Many temples are in ruins and some are locked; a local guide helps identify the important shrines.

name: Rikhia Ashram
description: Rikhia Ashram, about 9 km north of Deoghar, is a spiritual centre associated with Swami Satyananda Saraswati. It hosts a large Sat Chandi Mahayagya around Krishna Janmashtami and Sita Kalyan, drawing disciples from India and abroad.
how_to_reach: About 9 km north of Deoghar by road.
practical_notes: Events are large and time-specific; check the ashram's schedule and accommodation rules before visiting.

name: Deuridih Rural Tourism Village
description: Deuridih, in Kharsawan block of Saraikela Kharsawan district, is a rural tourism village in the state's tussar silk belt. Rows of arjun and asan trees feed silkworms, and visitors can see rearing, reeling and weaving as part of the village economy. It is about 54 km from Jamshedpur.
how_to_reach: About 54 km from Jamshedpur in Kharsawan block; reached by road.
practical_notes: This is a working village; arrange visits through the tourism department or a local host.
address: Deuridih Rural Tourism Village, Saraikela Kharsawan, Jharkhand

name: McCluskieganj
description: McCluskieganj, about 64 km northwest of Ranchi, is a small hilly town founded in the 1930s as a settlement for Anglo-Indian families. Its colonial bungalows, churches and quiet lanes give it an old-world atmosphere, and it is popular as a weekend retreat.
how_to_reach: About 64 km northwest of Ranchi by road.
practical_notes: Stay options are limited and best booked ahead; the town is best explored on foot.

name: Hirni Falls
description: Hirni Falls, about 70 km from Ranchi on the road to Chakradharpur, is formed by the Ramgarh river dropping around 121 feet in a forested setting. A path from the parking area leads to a tourist complex and a hilltop viewpoint over the fall and the surrounding forest.
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Ranchi via Chakradharpur in West Singhbhum district.
practical_notes: The walk involves steps and uneven ground; carry water and avoid the rocks during heavy flow.

name: Pahari Temple
description: Pahari Temple sits on Ranchi Hill, about 8 km from Ranchi railway station. The hill rises roughly 300 feet and a Shiva temple at the top is reached by 410 steps. The hill was used for hangings during British rule and was known as Phansi Tungri.
how_to_reach: About 8 km from Ranchi railway station via Ratu Road.
practical_notes: The climb is steep; mornings and evenings are cooler. The temple is busy during Shravan.

name: Ranchi Lake
description: Ranchi Lake, the city's largest water body, lies close to Ranchi Main Road and was built by Colonel Onsley in 1842. Spread over about 50 acres, it is a central landmark, though boating is no longer available.
how_to_reach: About 4 km from Ranchi railway station and 7 km from Birsa Munda airport.
practical_notes: The lake is best visited in the morning; avoid isolated corners after dark.

name: Rock Garden, Ranchi
description: Rock Garden on Kanke Road, about 8 km from Ranchi railway station, is built among the boulders of Gonda Hill. Artificial waterfalls, a hanging bridge and a bhoot bangla are the main attractions, and the garden looks over Kanke Dam.
how_to_reach: About 8 km from Ranchi railway station on Kanke Road.
practical_notes: The paths are uneven and stepped; wear comfortable shoes and allow an hour or more.

name: Kanke Dam
description: Kanke Dam in Ranchi spreads over about 8 sq km and supplies water to a large part of the city. It adjoins Gonda Hill and the Rock Garden, and a curved staircase over the water is a popular spot for sunrise and sunset views.
how_to_reach: About 8 km from Ranchi railway station and 12 km from the airport on Kanke Road.
practical_notes: The area is busiest at sunset; swimming is not permitted.

name: Tagore Hill
description: Tagore Hill, also called Morabadi Hill, is about 6 km from Ranchi and is associated with Jyotindranath Tagore, elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore. The hilltop offers views over the city and is a favoured spot for sunrise and sunset.
how_to_reach: About 6 km from central Ranchi at Morabadi.
practical_notes: The climb is short but steep in places; go with a companion after dark.

name: Jagannath Temple, Dhurwa
description: Jagannath Temple at Dhurwa, about 12 km from Ranchi, enshrines Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra. Built in 1691 by Nagvanshi ruler Thakur Ani Shahdeo and modelled on Odishan temple architecture, the 100-foot shrine hosts a large Rath Yatra fair in June-July.
how_to_reach: About 12 km from Ranchi in Dhurwa, near Hatia.
practical_notes: Rath Yatra draws big crowds; otherwise the temple is quiet and easy to visit.

name: Hundru Falls
description: Hundru Falls, about 45 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Purulia highway, is the highest fall in the Ranchi area, where the Subarnarekha river drops about 320 feet. The flow has powered the Sikidiri hydroelectric project for decades, and the fall is a short drive from the highway via Ormanjhi.
how_to_reach: About 45 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Purulia road, then about 10 km to Sikidiri.
practical_notes: Descend the steps carefully; the rocks are slippery and the current is dangerous.

name: Sita Falls
description: Sita Falls, about 40 km from Ranchi, is a lesser-known fall close to Jonha Falls. Water slides over rocky ledges in a series of small cascades, and the site is easily combined with a Jonha visit.
how_to_reach: Close to Jonha Falls; Jonha railway station is about 1.5-2 km away.
practical_notes: Facilities are basic; carry water and wear shoes with grip.

name: Deori Temple
description: Deori Temple, about 60 km from Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata highway, is dedicated to the sixteen-armed goddess Durga. It is the only temple in Jharkhand where worship is led for six days by a Pahan, the tribal priest, and for one day by traditional Brahmins.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Ranchi on NH-33; the temple is 3 km from Tamar in Deori village.
practical_notes: The temple is busiest during Durga Puja and Ram Navami; ask before photographing rituals.

name: Massanjore Dam
description: Massanjore Dam on the Mayurakshi river in Dumka district was completed in 1955 with Canadian assistance, and is also called Canada Dam or Pearson Dam. It is about 155 feet high and 2,170 feet long, and the reservoir is framed by two hills.
how_to_reach: In Dumka district, reached by road from Dumka; the dam is a short drive from the town.
practical_notes: The dam area is scenic after the monsoon; check whether the reservoir gates are open before visiting.

name: Moti Jharna
description: Moti Jharna, near Maharajpur in Sahebganj district, is a small waterfall and picnic spot fed by streams rising in the Rajmahal hills. It lies about 9.7 km from Maharajpur.
how_to_reach: About 9.7 km from Maharajpur in Sahebganj district by road.
practical_notes: The flow is seasonal; the site is at its best after the rains.

name: Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary
description: Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary, about 40 km from Sahebganj, comprises the two natural lakes of Pataura and Barail. The wetland hosts a large variety of resident birds and attracts migratory species in winter.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Sahebganj town by road.
practical_notes: Winter mornings are best for birdwatching; bring binoculars and keep a low profile near the water.
address: Udhwa Lake Bird Sanctuary, Sahebganj, Jharkhand

name: Maithon Dam
description: Maithon Dam on the Barakar river in Dhanbad district was completed in 1958. It is about 56 metres high and 4,357 metres long, and its underground power station was the first of its kind in South-East Asia. Boating on the reservoir makes it a popular day trip from Dhanbad.
how_to_reach: In Dhanbad district, reached by road from Dhanbad and Asansol.
practical_notes: Boating and access to the dam area depend on the season and security rules; check locally.

name: Topchanchi Lake
description: Topchanchi Lake lies in a small sanctuary of about 8.75 sq km on the Giridih-Dhanbad border, surrounded by hills. The lake and its forest shelter leopard, wild boar, langur and deer, and it is about 37 km from Dhanbad.
how_to_reach: About 37 km northwest of Dhanbad near Gomoh; autos and taxis run from Gomoh railway station.
practical_notes: The sanctuary is protected; stay on the road and do not feed or disturb animals.

name: Bhatinda Falls
description: Bhatinda Falls, about 15 km from Dhanbad, is formed by the Jamunia stream dropping roughly 10 metres over rocks. Its appeal lies in the broad spread of water across the rock face rather than height, and it is a popular Christmas and New Year picnic spot.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Dhanbad city and 25 km from Dhanbad railway station on the Dhanbad-Bokaro road (NH 32).
practical_notes: Very crowded on holidays; the rocks are slippery and there are no lifeguards.

name: Trikut Hills
description: Trikut Hills, about 16 km from Deoghar on the Deoghar-Dumka road, has three main peaks named after Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh. The hills contain caves used for worship, forest with elephants and deer, and a ropeway to the Vishnu peak.
how_to_reach: About 16 km from Deoghar on the Deoghar-Dumka road.
practical_notes: The ropeway may operate seasonally; check before relying on it and carry water for the climb.

name: Tapovan Hill
description: Tapovan Hill, about 10 km southwest of Deoghar, has a Shiva temple and caves once occupied by ascetics. Local tradition holds that Sita performed penance here.
how_to_reach: About 10 km southwest of Deoghar by road.
practical_notes: The site is quiet and undeveloped; go with a local driver who knows the approach road.

name: Itkhori
description: Itkhori in Chatra district, about 16 km west of Chauparan, is an archaeological site where Buddhist, Hindu and Jain remains sit together. The Bhadrakali temple complex here was built in the 9th century under Pala and Gupta patronage, and its carved sculptures show fine craftsmanship.
how_to_reach: About 16 km west of Chauparan in Chatra district; reached by road from Hazaribagh or Chatra.
practical_notes: The site is of active religious importance; dress modestly and ask before entering shrine areas.

name: Bhadrakali Temple, Bhaduli
description: Maa Bhadrakali Temple stands in Bhaduli village, about 1.5 km from Itkhori in Chatra district. The temple's image of the goddess is carved from a single rock, about four and a half feet high, and is believed to date to the Pala period. The complex includes a large yajna hall and a museum of sculptures found during excavation.
how_to_reach: About 1.5 km from Itkhori; reached by road from Chatra or Hazaribagh.
practical_notes: The museum may be closed on some days; check locally if you want to see the sculpture collection.

name: Dimna Lake
description: Dimna Lake, on the outskirts of Jamshedpur in East Singhbhum, is a reservoir at the foot of the Dalma hills. It supplies water to the city and is a popular spot for picnics and walks along the water.
how_to_reach: On the Jamshedpur-Chaibasa road, a short drive from the city.
practical_notes: Some areas around the lake are restricted as a water-supply zone; follow local signs.

name: Jubilee Park
description: Jubilee Park in Jamshedpur is a large landscaped park laid out in 1958 on land gifted by Tata Steel. Fountains, lawns and a lake make it a central recreation space, and it is especially lively during the winter festival.
how_to_reach: In central Jamshedpur, easily reached by auto or taxi.
practical_notes: The park is busiest in the evening; check opening hours during festivals.

name: Rankini Temple
description: Rankini Temple stands near Jadugoda on the Hata-Jadugoda road in East Singhbhum, about 3 km from Jadugoda and 35 km from Tatanagar. The shrine is dedicated to Kali and is believed to have once received human sacrifices, a practice stopped by the British in 1865.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from Jadugoda and 35 km from Tatanagar railway station.
practical_notes: The temple is an active place of worship; follow local customs and ask before photographing.

name: Upper Ghaghri Falls
description: Upper Ghaghri Falls is about 4 km from Netarhat, where water released from the dam forms a small fall between the Garitam and Ghaghri hills. The surrounding forest has chir, sal and deodar trees, and a large guava orchard lies nearby.
how_to_reach: About 4 km from Netarhat bus stand by road and a short walk.
practical_notes: The fall is small but the forest setting is the attraction; combine it with Lower Ghaghri.

name: Suga Bandh Falls
description: Suga Bandh Falls lies near Barsand in Latehar district, close to the Palamu Tiger Reserve and about 60 km from Betla. The stream drops through a forested ravine in a remote part of the district.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Betla in Latehar district; road access is limited and a local guide is advisable.
practical_notes: This is a remote site with few facilities; carry food, water and a charged phone.

name: Chandil Dam
description: Chandil Dam on the Subarnarekha river in Saraikela Kharsawan district was built in 1990 for industrial water supply and has since become a tourist spot. The dam is about 220 metres long, and the reservoir stretches to the horizon. It is about 40 km from Jamshedpur and 5 km from NH-33.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Jamshedpur and 5 km from NH-33.
practical_notes: Boating and lakeside facilities operate seasonally; weekends are busy.

name: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary covers the Dalma hills above Jamshedpur and is known for its elephant population, along with leopard, sloth bear and deer. The forested ridge rises steeply from the city and offers viewpoints over the plains.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Jamshedpur; the main gate is reached by road via Dimna.
practical_notes: Entry and safari arrangements are handled by the forest department; elephant sightings are never guaranteed.
address: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, East Singhbum, Jharkhand

name: Hazaribagh National Park
description: Hazaribagh National Park protects a hilly, forested tract in Hazaribagh district, with sal and bamboo woodland and populations of leopard, sambar, nilgai and wild boar. Watchtowers and forest roads allow wildlife viewing, and the park is a short drive from Hazaribagh town.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Hazaribagh town by road.
practical_notes: Safaris are best in the early morning; check forest department timings and vehicle rules.

name: Suraj Kund Hot Spring
description: Suraj Kund is a hot spring about 72 km southwest of Hazaribagh, where water emerges at around 190 degrees Fahrenheit. The spring is visited by people seeking relief from skin ailments, and the site has bathing arrangements.
how_to_reach: About 72 km southwest of Hazaribagh by road.
practical_notes: The water is very hot; test the temperature before bathing and follow local advice.
address: Suraj Kund Hot Spring, Hazaribagh, Jharkhand

name: Megaliths of Hazaribagh
description: The megaliths near Barkagaon, about 25 km from Hazaribagh, are a group of large stones arranged for astronomical observation. Two prominent stones are positioned to mark the equinox, and the site is regarded as an early sky-observation laboratory.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Hazaribagh near Barkagaon.
practical_notes: The stones are unprotected and in farmland; visit with a local guide and do not climb on them.

name: Maa Chhinnamasta Temple
description: Maa Chhinnamasta Temple at Rajrappa, about 65 km from Ranchi in Ramgarh district, stands at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhera rivers. The shrine is known for its image of the goddess without a head, seated on a lotus over Kamadeva and Rati, and draws pilgrims from Jharkhand, Bihar and West Bengal.
how_to_reach: About 65 km from Ranchi in Ramgarh district; reached by road via Ramgarh.
practical_notes: The temple is busy on Tuesdays and during Navaratri; be careful at the river ghats.

name: Patratu Dam
description: Patratu Dam in Ramgarh district stores water from the Nalkari river and lies beyond the town known for its thermal power plant. The reservoir is framed by sal forest, and the winding Patratu valley road has made it a popular drive and picnic destination.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Ranchi via Patratu; the valley road is the scenic approach.
practical_notes: The dam area is best visited in the cooler months; check local rules before going near the water.

name: Usri Falls
description: Usri Falls, about 13 km east of Giridih on the Tundi road, is formed by the Usri river dropping about 40 feet into a rocky pool and splitting into three streams. The fall is surrounded by the forests of the Parasnath hills and has a watchtower with a view of the southern hills.
how_to_reach: About 13 km east of Giridih on the Tundi road; the nearest railway station is Giridih.
practical_notes: The rocks are slippery and there are no lifeguards; the site is crowded at Christmas and New Year.

name: Anjan Gram
description: Anjan Gram, about 18 km from Gumla via Toto, is a village bounded by the Netarhat hills and the Khatwa river. It is believed to be the birthplace of Lord Hanuman and is named after his mother Anjani, with an ancient statue of Anjani at the site.
how_to_reach: About 18 km from Gumla via Toto and 130 km from Ranchi.
practical_notes: The village is a place of pilgrimage; dress modestly and ask before entering shrine areas.

name: State Museum, Ranchi
description: The State Museum in Hotwar, Ranchi, opened in 2009 to give Jharkhand's cultural, historical and artistic heritage a dedicated home. Its galleries cover tribal life, archaeology, art and the state's mineral wealth, building on the older Ranchi Museum established in 1974.
how_to_reach: At Hotwar in Ranchi, reached by road from the city centre.
practical_notes: Museums in Ranchi are generally closed on Mondays; confirm timings before visiting.

name: Indra Falls
description: Indra Falls in Tubed village, Latehar district, is a perennial waterfall where a hill stream drops about 30 feet into a pool. Dense forest surrounds the fall, and Tubed cave and Tatha Pani are nearby.
how_to_reach: In Tubed village, Latehar district; reached by road from Latehar with a short walk.
practical_notes: The fall flows year-round, but the approach can be muddy in the monsoon; go with a local guide.

name: Kanti Falls
description: Kanti Falls lies in Senha village, about 47 km from Latehar and 66 km from Ranchi, reached via a 7-km detour from the Ranchi-Medininagar road. The fall drops more than 200 feet and is at its most impressive during the monsoon.
how_to_reach: About 47 km from Latehar; turn off the Ranchi-Medininagar road near Senha.
practical_notes: The flow is strongest in the rains, when paths are slippery; keep a safe distance from the edge.

name: Magnolia Sunset Point
description: Magnolia Sunset Point, about 10 km from Netarhat, is named after a local story of an English officer's daughter and a shepherd whose flute she loved. The point looks west over the plateau and is one of Netarhat's best places to watch the sun go down.
how_to_reach: About 10 km from Netarhat by road.
practical_notes: Arrive before sunset and carry a light for the walk back; the road is narrow.

name: Sarju Valley
description: Sarju Valley lies in Garu block of Latehar district, about 20 km from Garu and 25 km from Latehar. It is a forested valley on the alternative Latehar-Netarhat route, with views over the surrounding hills.
how_to_reach: About 25 km from Latehar via the Latehar-Sarju road.
practical_notes: Facilities are minimal; travel in daylight with a local driver.

name: Nakshatra Van
description: Nakshatra Van in Ranchi is a landscaped garden planned around the twenty-seven nakshatras of Indian astronomy, with planting and spaces linked to the constellations. It is a quiet green space in the city and is used for nature education.
how_to_reach: In Ranchi near the Kanke Road area; reached by auto or taxi.
practical_notes: Best visited in the morning or evening; check local opening hours.

name: Luguburu Ghantabari
description: Luguburu Ghantabari, on Lugu hill in Gomia block of Bokaro district, is a pilgrimage site of the Santhal community. The Lugu Baba temple sits among hills, forests and waterfalls, and the largest Santhal religious gathering is held here on Kartik Purnima.
how_to_reach: In Gomia block, Bokaro district; reached by road from Bokaro or Gomia.
practical_notes: The Kartik Purnima gathering is very large; arrange transport and accommodation well in advance.

name: Lavapani Falls
description: Lavapani Falls in Peshrar block of Lohardaga district is about 36 km from Lohardaga and 25 km from Latehar. The stream descends in roughly twelve steps from east to west rather than in a single drop, creating a series of distinct cascades in dense forest.
how_to_reach: About 36 km from Lohardaga via Kekarang and Peshrar; about 112 km from Ranchi.
practical_notes: The last stretch is remote and rough; a local guide is recommended.

name: Hatia Dam
description: Hatia Dam, despite its name, lies in the Dhurwa area of Ranchi and spreads over about 7 sq km. It supplies water to a large population, and its stone-pitched slope, gazebos and calm water make it a popular spot for an evening walk and sunset view.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from central Ranchi in Dhurwa.
practical_notes: Swimming is not officially supervised; stay on the paved areas and follow local rules.

name: Tanginath
description: Tanginath is an old Shiva temple site in Gumla district, reached from Majhgaon. The shrine is set among forest and hills and is associated with local Shaiva tradition.
how_to_reach: In Gumla district near Majhgaon; reached by road from Gumla.
practical_notes: The site is quiet and rural; carry water and check the road condition locally.

name: Biodiversity Park, Ranchi
description: Biodiversity Park in Ranchi is a green space developed to showcase the state's plant diversity, with labelled species, nurseries and walking paths. It is used for environmental education and quiet recreation.
how_to_reach: In Ranchi, reached by road from the city centre.
practical_notes: Go early for birds and cooler walking; check opening days.

name: Maa Ugratara Temple
description: Maa Ugratara Temple in Latehar district is about 37 km from Latehar town and 90 km from Ranchi. The temple is believed to have been built in the tenth century by the royal family of Tori, and it is held that wishes made here are fulfilled. Worship is shared by the royal and Mishra families.
how_to_reach: About 37 km from Latehar near Tori; reached by road.
practical_notes: The temple is busy at Ram Navami and Durga Puja; follow local customs regarding offerings.

name: Netarhat Dam
description: Netarhat Dam, about 1.5-2 km from Netarhat bus stand, dates from the British period and still supplies water to the area. The reservoir spreads over about 4 sq km against a backdrop of pines and hills, and is used for picnics, boating and fishing.
how_to_reach: About 1.5-2 km from Netarhat bus stand.
practical_notes: Boating depends on water levels and local arrangements; the lake is a good spot for a quiet morning.

name: Koel River View Point
description: Koel River View Point is about 2 km from Netarhat bus stand, reached through chir pine forest. The Koel river flows far below, and the point is known for dawn and dusk views as the water reflects the changing sky.
how_to_reach: About 2 km from Netarhat bus stand by road and a short walk.
practical_notes: The light is best at sunrise and sunset; carry a torch for the return walk.
address: Koel River View Point, Latehar, Jharkhand

name: Chalet House, Netarhat
description: Chalet House in Netarhat is a historic building made of wooden logs, built in the early twentieth century during the time of Sir Edward Gait, Lieutenant Governor of Bihar and Orissa. It was used as a summer retreat for discussions with local chiefs and now serves as the camp office of the Latehar Deputy Commissioner.
how_to_reach: In Netarhat town, a short walk or drive from the bus stand.
practical_notes: It is an administrative building; view it from outside and do not enter without permission.

name: Tattapani Hot Water Spring
description: Tattapani Hot Water Spring lies in Jagram village, about 11 km from Latehar. The sulphur-rich water is believed to have medicinal value, especially for the skin, and is used by locals and visitors for bathing.
how_to_reach: About 11 km from Latehar in Jagram village.
practical_notes: The water is hot and sulphurous; test it first and avoid bathing if you have open cuts.
address: Tattapani Hot Water Spring, Latehar, Jharkhand

name: Sun Temple, Giridih
description: The Sun Temple in Giridih is built in the middle of a lake in the shape of a lotus, with a statue of Surya seated on a chariot drawn by seven horses. Other shrines in the complex honour Lakshmi Narayan, Rama, Sita, Hanuman, Shiva, Parvati, Gayatri, Radha and Krishna. The site was earlier known as Sita Ni Chauri and Ramkund.
how_to_reach: In Giridih town, reached by road from the bus stand or railway station.
practical_notes: The temple is photogenic in the morning; check local timings and footwear rules.

name: Shakti Mandir
description: Shakti Mandir on Thorapathak Road in the heart of Dhanbad is dedicated to Durga. The temple is known for its Akhand Jyoti, an eternal flame brought from Vaishno Devi, and draws devotees especially on Tuesdays, Fridays, Diwali and Dussehra.
how_to_reach: In central Dhanbad on Thorapathak Road; autos and taxis are readily available.
practical_notes: The temple is crowded on Tuesdays and Fridays; leave footwear outside and follow queue rules.

name: Harihar Dham
description: Harihar Dham on the Hazaribagh-Bagodar road in Giridih district is home to a Shivling believed to be the largest in the country. The temple, built in the shape of a Shivling, stands 65 feet tall and was constructed in 1987 by Pandit Amarnath Mukhopadhyay, a former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court. A Radha-Krishna temple and a marriage hall are within the premises.
how_to_reach: On NH-100 on the Hazaribagh-Bagodar road in Giridih district; reached by road from Giridih or Hazaribagh.
practical_notes: The temple is busy through Shravan; allow time for the crowds and parking.

name: Ulihatu
description: Ulihatu in Khunti district is the birthplace of Birsa Munda, the tribal leader and freedom fighter born here on 15 November 1875. The village, about 37 km north of Khunti and 80 km from Ranchi, sits among hills and has an unexplored sunset point nearby.
how_to_reach: About 37 km north of Khunti and 80 km from Ranchi by road.
practical_notes: The village is of great historical importance; ask locally before photographing homes and residents.

name: Sidhu and Kanhu Park
description: Sidhu and Kanhu Park in Ranchi commemorates the Murmu brothers who led the Santhal rebellion of the 1850s against colonial rule and the zamindari system. The central park has lawns, children's rides, an open gym and a small toy train.
how_to_reach: A few kilometres from Ranchi railway station in the heart of the city.
practical_notes: The park is liveliest in the evening; the toy train runs on a small ticket.
address: Sidhu and Kanhu Park, Ranchi, Jharkhand

name: Ranchi Science Centre
description: Ranchi Science Centre is a science museum with interactive exhibits on physics, energy, the human body and the natural world, aimed at students and families. It is part of the state's science education network.
how_to_reach: In Ranchi, reached by road from the city centre.
practical_notes: Check show timings for the planetarium and galleries; school holidays are busiest.

name: Palna Dam
description: Palna Dam lies about 2 km off NH-33 near Palna village, about 15 km from Chandil towards Ranchi. Built by the water resources department, it is an older dam that is being renovated, with boating planned, and it forms part of the Chandil-Dalma-Burudih tourism circuit.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Chandil towards Ranchi on NH-33, then 2 km off the highway.
practical_notes: Facilities are limited while renovation work continues; check the current status locally.

name: Lapung Sai Temple
description: Lapung Sai Temple in Ranchi district has become a centre of faith for large numbers of devotees. The site also has an ancient Shiva temple, giving it religious and historical importance, and the Sai Mahotsav is held here.
how_to_reach: At Lapung in Ranchi district, reached by road from Ranchi.
practical_notes: The temple is busiest during the Sai Mahotsav; check dates locally before planning.

name: Patratu Valley
description: Patratu Valley in Ramgarh district is a hill town at about 1,300 feet above sea level, known for its winding ghat road, forested slopes and views over the Patratu reservoir. It is a popular weekend drive from Ranchi and is also known for the Patratu power plant.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Ranchi via Patratu; the valley road is the scenic route.
practical_notes: The road has sharp bends and is busy on weekends; drive carefully and avoid stopping in blind corners.

name: Kaitha Shiv Mandir
description: Kaitha Shiv Mandir in Ramgarh was built in 1670 after Raja Dalel Singh of Padma moved his capital to Ramgarh. A cave below the temple is said to hold the power of Kaithashwari Devi, which gives the shrine its name. The architecture blends Mughal, Bengali and Rajput styles, and the temple is 3 km from Ramgarh town on NH-23.
how_to_reach: About 3 km from Ramgarh town on the Gola road (NH-23).
practical_notes: The temple is an active place of worship; the cave steps are narrow, so take care.

name: Chutupalu Valley
description: Chutupalu Valley lies on the Ranchi-Hazaribagh road where the highway descends through forested hills. The valley is known for its views, cool air and roadside stops, and it is a common break on the drive between Ranchi and Hazaribagh.
how_to_reach: On the Ranchi-Hazaribagh road in Ranchi district.
practical_notes: Traffic moves fast on the highway; stop only at designated lay-bys and keep valuables secure.

name: Jain Museum, Madhuban
description: The Jain Museum at Madhuban in Giridih district, near the base of Parasnath hill, displays historic idols, stamps on Jain Tirthankaras, architectural models, literature and photographs of Jain temples across India. Its ivory symbols are a notable part of the collection, and the museum is a quiet stop for pilgrims and students of Jainism.
how_to_reach: At Madhuban, about 11 km from Parasnath railway station and 35 km from Giridih.
practical_notes: The museum is connected with the Parasnath pilgrimage; check timings before climbing the hill.

name: Tomb of Shaheed Sheikh Bhikhari
description: The tomb and samadhi of Shaheed Sheikh Bhikhari, a leader of the 1857 uprising in Chotanagpur, stands at Chutupalu on the Ranchi-Hazaribagh road. Sheikh Bhikhari was a commander in the revolt and is remembered as a martyr of the region.
how_to_reach: At Chutupalu on the Ranchi-Hazaribagh road.
practical_notes: The site is a roadside memorial; visit in daylight and keep the area clean.
address: Tomb of Shaheed Sheikh Bhikhari, Ranchi, Jharkhand

name: Yogoda Satsanga Sakha Math
description: Yogoda Satsanga Sakha Math in Ranchi is a branch of the Yogoda Satsanga Society of India, the organisation founded by Paramahansa Yogananda. The ashram offers meditation, satsangs and retreats in a quiet garden setting.
how_to_reach: In Ranchi, reached by road from the city centre.
practical_notes: Visitors are welcome for meditation and satsang; check the ashram's schedule and silence rules.
address: Yogoda Satsanga Sakha Math, Ranchi, Jharkhand
